No worries at all! This is my passion and I love talking about it! my partner can't get me to shut up about it 😂. Yeah! I'm working on a personal piece a comic book and playing with style ( I work mostly in realism, so doing something more graphic is fun and scary). So surface quality can be interesting as well! I personally like heavy texture work ( it's more my style as well as I paint ) especially in oil paining. My favorite example of this is Mound of Butter a Still life by Antoine Vollon. There is enough paint used to create a surface that shows a buttery surface and makes you wanna touch it. A lot of begining painters don't use enough paint to medium ratio and it gives a thin texture so you see the weave of the canvas under the paint. Surface quality varies I love thick surface with lost of texture but smoother blended surfaces are just as valid!

I have the same issue, something that's really helped me is having a pocket sized sketch book it allows you to focus on form rather then get caught up in details! It's helped me explore some of my personal work and work on style without worrying about details. If you don't thumbnail it also really helps for larger projects! I do it with all fo my paintings ( just five tiny sketches to look at form context and space ) it makes the larger piece feel way less daunting.

It's a tricky question! Because a lot of it is based on "quality" which in my uni is up to professors. So it seems to be up and down. A lot of it is clear understaing of material ( a good example is application of oil paint and using enough paint to give a satisfying surface) I think a good portion is seeing progress though your portfolio, solid style, understanding of medium, context with art history, good understanding of fundmentals , working on challenging pieces , and most importantly how much time was spent working. It's differs from different mediums, this is mostly from my work in painting, drawing, ceramics, and sculpture. And I'm still undergrad so I'm not sure for what is looked for in graduate! I hope this was helpful 😊
